..
Friday afternoon through Saturday: Current observations this morning 
reflects a tight moisture gradient from the east slopes of the 
Washington Cascades where dew points have dropped in the teens to 
the Idaho Panhandle where dew points are in the low 40s. The 
prognoses is for this dry air to continue to punch across the region 
with decreasing cloud over expected over the Idaho Panhandle. Winds 
have also picked up and are gusty out of the north through the 
Okanogan Valley with gusts of 25-35 mph common. The north winds 
extend across the Waterville Plateau and into the western portion of 
the Columbia Basin. The northerly gradient will relax into this 
afternoon with wind speeds gradually relaxing and will become light 
overnight. This evening till midnight will see clear skies and light 
winds. Strong radiational cooling is expected over this period. An 
upper level low will also migrate off of the Washington coast 
tonight. High clouds will then start to push across the Cascades 
into eastern Washington and this is expected to slow the radiative 
cooling process. There is some uncertainty with the low temperatures 
tonight as the cloud cover will have an impact, but model guidance 
is consistent with much of the region seeing near to or below 
freezing temperatures. There have been some spots in the Moses Lake 
Area in the Lewiston-Clarkston Valley that have already had their 
first freeze of the season, but not all locations. A freeze warning 
has been issued as confidence is high that these zones at the end of 
their growing season will see freezing temperatures tonight. It will 
be dry enough for the Wenatchee Area to radiate to near freezing, 
but the increasing high clouds should make areas there have a harder 
time to hit freezing. It was decided to issue a frost advisory as 
low temperatures are expected to bottom out in the low 30s near to 
or just above freezing. Plants susceptible to frost or freeze damage 
should take action today to cover them or bring them inside to 
protect from damage overnight.

Saturday night through Tuesday night: The upper low pressure system 
that develops will eject inland during this period. Where the center 
of the low tracks is still a bit uncertain, but the majority of
the model ensembles tracks the low somewhere between southern 
Washington to northern California. The majority of the GEFS 
ensemble members takes the more southerly route, whereas the 
ECMWF Ensemble is further north. Even the ECMWF Ensemble 
doesn't spread much precipitaiton across the region for two 
reasons: (1) we are starting out dry and (2) this low won't tap
into a good moisture source like the low that is pushing across
the northern Rockies today. The National Blend of Models has 
low end chances for measuring up to a 30- 60% chance across 
southeast Washington into the southern Idaho Panhandle. The 
wetter envelop of potential solutions gives this portion of the 
region between a tenth to a quarter of an inch of precipitation 
from Monday through Tuesday. Snow levels lower to around 6,000 
feet falling mostly as rain except for light snow at over the 
highest mountain peaks.

Wednesday through Friday: Model uncertainty and spread in potential 
scenarios increases for the latter half of next week. Early 
indications is that there will be another upper level low that 
develops in the wake of the low pressure system early in the 
week. Roughly 50% of the model ensemble spread has the low 
developing in close proximity, if not right over Washington by 
Wednesday night into Thursday. Then there is the other 50% that 
digs energy further south with the center of the low closer in 
proximity to Oregon or California. Like the upper low early in 
the week, this one later in the week doesn't look to tap into a 
good moisture source. Any precipitation that is generated by 
this upper low will likely bring limited precipitation. Snow 
levels are expected to be a bit lower down to 3,000 to 4,500 
feet and may generate a dusting of snow in the mountains. 
Confidence is higher that temperatures will remain at least near
average, if not slightly cooler than normal if the upper low 
does decide to pass more so over the region. /SVH
